brief: {"brief":["Approach: Async decision memos with a fixed comment window and named decider; evidence: commonly reported practitioner practice.","Approach: Explicit decision rights plus a lightweight decision log; evidence: commonly reported remote-operations case reports.","Approach: Silent written pre-mortems or red-team rounds before commitment; evidence: commonly reported, with mixed field-experiment support.","Limitation: Memos can become documentation theater and favor fluent writers; evidence: practitioner case reports.","Limitation: Logs decay without owner review and can hide unresolved disagreement; evidence: commonly reported.","Strongest criticism: The mainstream treats decisions as information problems, but many are power/trust problems; async artifacts may entrench hierarchy.","Analogy: Aviation checklists reduce missed steps without adding meetings, but only when roles and go/no-go authority are clear."]}
